correctness.rationale: For squarefree n, sigma_{-2}(n)=product_{p|n}(1+p^{-2}). The positive log factors for primes >=5 are summable. Verified each of the eight exact rational product certificates for p=5,7,11,13,17,19,23,29: the exhibited finite Q_p tail product exceeds 1+p^{-2}. For p>=31, the stated explicit prime-counting lower bound pi(2p)-pi(p)>3p/(5 log p) implies at least six primes q in (p,2p], and log(1+q^{-2}) >=1/(4p²)-1/(32p^4) implies the total later logs exceed log(1+p^{-2}). The overlapping-tail subsum lemma then fills exactly a continuous interval of possible infinite subsums; finite squarefree products are dense therein. From Euler product zeta(2)/zeta(4)=15/pi², the >=5 tail endpoint is 54/(5pi²); independent multipliers 1,10/9,5/4,25/18 for primes 2,3 give exactly the four displayed pairwise disjoint closed intervals. Independent rational checks verify all finite certificates and separations. Infinite coverage relies on the cited valid prime-density bound and subsum proof, not enumeration.
